Segment RT passes through the center P, so PR and PT are opposite rays, and RT is a diameter. The central angle ∠QPT is marked as 112° in the figure, and PS is a radius; the problem gives PS=4. Reasoning: What is required is the length of minor arc QR, whose corresponding central angle is ∠QPR. Because PR and PT are opposite rays, ∠QPR and ∠QPT form a linear pair and sum to 180°. Therefore ∠QPR = 180° - 112° = 68°. The radius r=PS=4. The arc length formula is s = (θ/360°)·2πr, so s = (68/360)·2π·4 ≈ 4.75. Rounded to the hundredths place, it is 4.75.

raw_record.question_text: In $\odot P$, $PS=4$, find the length of $\widehat{QR}$. Round to the nearest hundredth.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a circle centered at P. From the image, R, P, and T lie on one straight diameter, and the central angle between PQ and PT is labeled 112°. The requested arc QR is the minor arc intercepted by central angle QPR. Because PR and PT are opposite rays, ∠QPR and ∠QPT form a linear pair, so ∠QPR = 180° - 112° = 68°. From the text, PS = 4, so the radius is 4. Use the arc length formula s = (θ/360°)·2πr: s = (68/360)·2π·4 ≈ 4.75.
